deep.reconstruction:
CONTEXT. This page is a working draft of the end of Riemann's Göttingen dissertation (1851), 'Grundlagen für eine allgemeine Theorie der Functionen einer veränderlichen complexen Grösse'. The left column belongs to the Dirichlet-principle part (Art. 16-18). The right column is an outline of the closing articles. Its headings agree with the printed text:
- Art. 20: the origin of complex quantities in the theory of simple dependence laws expressed by operations on quantities.
- Art. 21: the mapping theorem, given as an illustration of the general theorems.
- Art. 22: Schlussbemerkungen.

PROBLEM (left column). We minimise the Dirichlet integral L = ∬_T (λ_x² + λ_y²) dx dy over admissible functions λ. Riemann must show that λ cannot tend to a limit σ with a non-removable discontinuity while L stays finite. Two kinds of discontinuity are considered:
- (a) σ is discontinuous along a line;
- (b) σ is singular at a point O', in the sense that on part of a small circle of radius ϱ about O' the quantities ϱ ∂σ/∂ϱ (and the angular derivative) tend to a finite nonzero limit or become infinite as ϱ→0.

The reformulation is as follows. Require λ = σ outside a region T' that contains the discontinuities. Then T' can be chosen so small that L > C for any prescribed C, however λ is chosen inside T'.

(b) POINT CASE. Use polar coordinates (ϱ, φ) about O'. Choose R so that the angular quantity ϱ² ∫_0^{2π} |∇σ|² dφ does not vanish for ϱ < R, and let a > 0 be its minimum on the interval. The manuscript seems to show a single ϱ in front of the integral; the inequality only works with ϱ², see Errors.

The annulus r < ϱ < R contributes to L:
∫_r^R dϱ ∫_0^{2π} |∇λ|² ϱ dφ = ∫_r^R (1/ϱ)·[ϱ² ∫ |∇λ|² dφ] dϱ ≥ ∫_r^R (a/ϱ) dϱ = a (log R − log r).

This exceeds C once r = R e^{−C/a}. So take T' to be a disc of radius ϱ < R e^{−C/a}. On the annulus λ = σ, so the part of L coming from the rest of T, and hence L itself, exceeds C whatever λ is inside the disc. This is a logarithmic-capacity argument: the annulus has conformal modulus log(R/r).

(a) LINE CASE. Use curvilinear coordinates along a continuously curved arc of the discontinuity line:
- s is arc length and p is the signed normal distance;
- κ(s) is the curvature;
- p_1, p_2 are the values of p on the boundary of T' (a strip about the line), and σ_1, σ_2 the corresponding values of σ.

The area element is (1 − κp) dp ds and |∇λ|² = λ_p² + λ_s²/(1 − κp)². This requires 1 − κp > 0, i.e. the strip must not reach the centres of curvature; this condition is inserted in the margin. The part of T' between the end normals contributes
∫ ds ∫_{p_2}^{p_1} [λ_p² + λ_s²/(1 − κp)²] (1 − κp) dp.

The first, struck-out attempt drops the weight (1 − κp) and uses the fact that, for fixed end values, ∫ λ_p² dp is least when λ_p is constant. This gives the bound ∫ ds ∫ ((σ_2 − σ_1)/(p_2 − p_1))² dp = ∫ (σ_2 − σ_1)²/(p_2 − p_1) ds.

The next page does it correctly with the weight. My Cauchy–Schwarz derivation:
(Δλ)² ≤ ∫ λ_p² (1 − κp) dp · ∫ dp/(1 − κp),
which gives
min ∫_{p_2}^{p_1} λ_p² (1 − κp) dp = κ (λ_1 − λ_2)² / [log(1 − κp_2) − log(1 − κp_1)].
The minimiser is λ linear in log(1 − κp).

As p_1 → 0+ and p_2 → 0−, the denominator ~ κ(p_1 − p_2) → 0. The jump λ_1 − λ_2 stays bounded away from 0, so the contribution exceeds any C for a thin enough strip. The next page also notes that removable singularities can have finite energy, e.g. (log 1/ϱ)^α with α < 1/2, and modifies the minimum theorem accordingly.

RIGHT COLUMN. Art. 21 states the theorem: every simply connected surface can be mapped onto every simply connected surface, continuously and similar in the smallest parts (i.e. conformally). The map is unique once the image of one interior point and of one boundary point is prescribed. This is the Riemann mapping theorem as stated in the dissertation.
errors: The prefactor in the point case: as transcribed, ϱ∫|∇λ|²dφ ≥ a would give ∫a dϱ, not ∫(a/ϱ)dϱ. The step to a(log R − log r) needs ϱ²∫|∇λ|²dφ ≥ a, i.e. ∫|∇λ|² ϱ dφ ≥ a/ϱ. Either the manuscript has ϱ² (hard to read) or this is a slip.

The exponent of the critical radius: on the image the exponent appears to read a/C (and possibly lacks a minus sign). The correct value is r = R e^{−C/a}, since a log(R/r) > C ⟺ r < R e^{−C/a}. Possibly a slip, or a misreading of the faint writing.

The struck-out line-case bound ignores the weight (1 − κp). It is also inconsistent in orientation (∫_{p_2}^{p_1} above, ∫_{p_1}^{p_2} with p_2 − p_1 below), so the sign of (σ_2 − σ_1)²/(p_2 − p_1) depends on convention. Riemann crossed it out and replaced it on the next page with the correct weighted minimum.

The point-case argument assumes λ = σ on the annulus r < ϱ < R, i.e. T' lies inside the small disc. This is implicit but consistent with the setup. The condition on 'a part of the circle' then requires a to be defined from the integral over that arc, which is not spelled out.

Unjustified in a modern sense: the whole surrounding argument presupposes that a minimiser of the Dirichlet integral exists (the Dirichlet principle), which Weierstrass later criticised. The local estimates on this page are themselves correct.

results.what: Lower bound a·log(R/r) for the Dirichlet energy on an annulus around a point singularity with ϱ∂σ/∂ϱ not tending to 0; hence such singularities force infinite energy
results.modern_name: Logarithmic capacity / conformal modulus estimate for annuli (energy of point singularities)
results.usually_credited_to: Riemann (1851 dissertation, Art. 17); capacity theory later (Wiener, Fekete, etc.)

results.what: Dirichlet energy in normal (s,p) coordinates along a curve with curvature κ; weighted 1D minimum κ(Δλ)²/[log(1−κp_2) − log(1−κp_1)] showing jump discontinuities along a line force infinite energy
results.modern_name: Euler–Lagrange / Cauchy–Schwarz minimisation in Fermi coordinates; non-existence of finite-energy functions with jumps (H^1 functions have no jump discontinuities)

results.what: Outline of Art. 20–22, including the statement of the conformal mapping theorem with uniqueness normalisation (one interior and one boundary point)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a draft of material printed almost verbatim in Riemann's 1851 dissertation (Art. 17 on singularities in the Dirichlet principle, and Art. 20–22 including the mapping theorem). It is of interest for the genesis of the text, e.g. the struck-out unweighted bound, but contains nothing not already known as his.

checkable.sympy: a,r,R=symbols('a r R',positive=True); simplify(integrate(a/rho,(rho,r,R)) - a*(log(R)-log(r)))  # rho=symbols('rho',positive=True)
checkable.asserts: The annulus bound ∫_r^R a/ϱ dϱ = a(log R − log r).
With r = R e^{−C/a} the bound equals exactly C, so smaller r gives > C (correct exponent is −C/a).
Example σ = φ (angle): |∇σ| = 1/ϱ, energy on the annulus = 2π log(R/r) → ∞ as r → 0.

checkable.sympy: p,k,p1,p2,c=symbols('p k p1 p2 c'); lam=c*log(1-k*p); simplify(diff((1-k*p)*diff(lam,p),p))
checkable.asserts: λ = c·log(1−κp) satisfies the Euler–Lagrange equation d/dp[(1−κp)λ_p] = 0 for ∫λ_p²(1−κp)dp.

checkable.sympy: p,k,p1,p2,D=symbols('p k p1 p2 D',positive=True); c=D/(log(1-k*p1)-log(1-k*p2)); lam=c*log(1-k*p); simplify(integrate(diff(lam,p)**2*(1-k*p),(p,p2,p1)) - k*D**2/(log(1-k*p2)-log(1-k*p1)))
checkable.asserts: The weighted minimum ∫_{p2}^{p1} λ_p²(1−κp)dp equals κ(λ1−λ2)²/[log(1−κp2) − log(1−κp1)], with D the jump.
As κ → 0 the denominator/κ tends to p1 − p2, recovering the unweighted bound (Δσ)²/(p1 − p2) of the struck-out line.
Next-page example: energy of (log 1/ϱ)^α near 0 reduces to 2πα²∫t^{2α−2}dt, which converges iff α < 1/2.

transcription_corrections: 'ϱ dσ/dx' in the opening paragraph is most likely the angular derivative (dσ/dφ, possibly without ϱ) rather than dσ/dx; uncertain reading.
The prefactor before ∫_0^{2π}(...)dφ in the definition of a may be ϱ² rather than ϱ; mathematically ϱ² is required.
The exponent in 'r = R e^{...}' and 'ϱ < R e^{...}' appears on the image as a/C (fraction a over C); the transcription's −C/a is the mathematically correct value but may not be what is written.
'{+ausserhalb eines [?]+}' is an interlinear insertion above 'unterworfen'; it probably reads 'ausserhalb eines Flächentheils' or similar.

Art. 20 fragment: the struck-out words after 'Abhängigkeitsgesetze' include 'zwischen veränderlichen Grössen'-type wording, cf. the printed text 'Theorie einfacher durch Grössenoperationen ausgedrückter Abhängigkeitsgesetze zwischen veränderlichen Grössen'.
Art. 21: 'Als Beispiel zur Erläuterung der allgemeinen Sätze' ('zu' should probably read 'zur').
